claims.text: Increasing atomic-mass disparity modifies the vibrational density of states in high-entropy superconducting alloys.
Increasing atomic-mass disparity enhances low-energy phonon modes.
Differences in elastic constants are associated with atomic-mass disparity.
Enhanced low-energy phonon modes increase electron–phonon coupling strength.
Electron–phonon coupling directly governs the superconducting transition temperature in the proposed alloys.
Electron–phonon coupling is responsible for superconducting pairing in the proposed alloy system.
The proposed initial materials are single-phase CoCrFeMnNi-based high-entropy alloys with fixed average electron count and low mass disparity.
Single-element substitution can systematically vary mass disparity while electron count and phase stability remain constant.
Arc-melting can maintain a single-phase structure across the proposed compositional series.
Inelastic neutron scattering can characterize changes in the low-energy vibrational density of states.
Raman spectroscopy can characterize the proposed distinct low-energy phonon modes in these alloys.
Alloys with greater mass disparity should show a measurable shift or enhancement of low-energy phonon modes relative to low-disparity controls.
Changes in low-energy phonon modes should correlate systematically with changes in superconducting transition temperature.
The transition temperature may increase as mass disparity and low-energy phonon spectral weight increase.
Compositional modifications may independently alter local chemical ordering or electronic structure.
The proposed causal interpretation is restricted to single-phase, arc-melted alloys with constant electron count and controlled ordering, clustering, and residual strain.
A lack of consistent correlation between low-energy phonon changes and transition-temperature changes would falsify the hypothesis.
A stronger association of transition-temperature changes with ordering or clustering than with vibrational spectra would falsify the proposed phonon-mediated explanation.
